how_it_works: recovery-from-boot.p is a legacy AOSP non-A/B block-based-OTA mechanism, completely independent of AVB/dm-verity. On non-A/B devices (which this device is), an OTA updates /boot and /system in place but deliberately leaves /recovery untouched during the update itself, to avoid bricking if power is lost while writing the very partition the updater is running from. Instead, the new /system image ships /system/etc/install-recovery.sh (a oneshot service script) plus /system/recovery-from-boot.p (a bsdiff/imgdiff binary patch) and optionally /system/etc/recovery-resource.dat. Standard AOSP rootdir/init.rc (or, on split builds, vendor/etc/init/vendor_flash_recovery.rc) declares: `service flash_recovery /system/etc/install-recovery.sh` / `class main` / `oneshot`, triggered on a post-fs-data boot trigger during the FIRST normal boot after the update. install-recovery.sh runs `applypatch`, which (1) computes a hash of the current /recovery block device, (2) compares it to an expected target SHA1 baked into the script at build time, (3) if already matching, logs and exits (no-op), (4) if not, reconstructs a new recovery image from /boot (source) + recovery-from-boot.p (patch data) via applypatch/imgdiff, and writes the result directly to /dev/block/by-name/recovery. Results are logged via a vendor property and to /cache/recovery/last_install. The data flow is strictly (boot.img + recovery-from-boot.p) -> /recovery partition. There is no code path in this mechanism that reads a 'golden' /system image and writes it back into /system, and no code path that touches /system/etc/init/hw/init.rc at all -- it only ever produces or refreshes the /recovery partition, using /boot as its source.
fits_observed_symptoms: (1) Write succeeds and is confirmed pre-reboot: unaffected either way -- install-recovery.sh only fires during normal-boot post-fs-data processing, never while sitting in a manual Recovery session, so this is neutral evidence. (2) Survives unmount/remount within the same recovery session: trivially consistent, but only because the flash_recovery service can never run at all while parked in Recovery mode with /system loop-mounted -- this is true regardless of whether the mechanism exists on this build, so it is not real confirming evidence. (3) Reverts only after a real power-cycle boot: superficially matches 'requires an actual boot to fire,' but this precondition is satisfied by almost any boot-time init mechanism and is not unique to this one; it also does not matter because the mechanism's write target is /recovery, never /system. (4) The boot_completed marker-file write added to init.rc never appears in /cache: this is actually evidence AGAINST this mechanism being the (sole) cause -- it shows the entire init.rc text reverted before init ever parsed it, and recovery-from-boot.p/applypatch has no capability to rewrite /system/etc/init/hw/init.rc content; some other mechanism must be doing that. (5) AVB disabled (flags=2, unsigned): irrelevant -- this is a pre-AVB-era, pure-SHA1-hash-check mechanism, unaffected by vbmeta state either way. (6) /system is ext4 not squashfs: irrelevant -- the mechanism never inspects /system's filesystem type, only reads /boot and writes the /recovery block device directly. (7) Non-A/B device: this is a necessary precondition for the mechanism to exist at all (A/B devices don't ship install-recovery.sh/recovery-from-boot.p, they use slot switching instead), so its plausible presence here is consistent -- but necessary is not sufficient, and it still cannot explain the actual symptom. Overall: does not fit. This mechanism can be ruled out on architectural grounds alone (wrong write target: /recovery, not /system/init.rc), independent of any device-specific testing.
known_precedent: Extremely well-documented as a generic AOSP non-A/B OTA mechanism (source.android.com's non-A/B OTA docs, and install-recovery.sh/applypatch templates present verbatim across a huge number of OEM device trees -- Samsung, Motorola, and many others -- going back to early Android versions). It is commonly inherited by low-cost Android Go / STB / TV-box builds, including Rockchip-based ones, whenever they retain a discrete legacy /recovery partition rather than adopting Virtual A/B. No RK3326- or TXCZ-specific writeup, teardown, or forum thread confirming this exact mechanism's presence on this device family was found in public search results; its applicability here is inferred generically from standard AOSP inheritance, not confirmed by device-specific documentation. [uncertain]
likelihood: low -- recovery-from-boot.p/applypatch only ever writes to the /recovery block device using /boot + patch data as its source; it has no code path that reads from or restores into /system/etc/init/hw/init.rc, so it structurally cannot produce a text revert of init.rc no matter how well the surface timing symptoms (only-after-reboot) align.
test_procedure: All commands run from the existing Android Recovery root shell (adb root already available), with /system loop-mounted at whatever mount point your existing workflow uses (shown here as $SYS, e.g. /mnt/system): 1) Confirm whether the mechanism's required files even exist on this build -- if absent, the item is definitively dead with no further testing needed: `adb shell "ls -la $SYS/etc/install-recovery.sh $SYS/recovery-from-boot.p $SYS/etc/recovery-resource.dat 2>&1"` and `adb shell "ls -la /vendor/etc/install-recovery.sh /vendor/etc/init/vendor_flash_recovery.rc /vendor/bin/install-recovery.sh 2>&1"`. 2) Search the compiled (plain-text) init.rc and any vendor init fragments for the service definition: `adb shell "grep -n -A3 -E 'flash_recovery|install-recovery' $SYS/etc/init/hw/init.rc $SYS/etc/init/*.rc /vendor/etc/init/*.rc 2>/dev/null"`. 3) If present, verify it only ever touches /recovery, not /system, by hashing the recovery partition across a reboot cycle: `adb shell "sha1sum /dev/block/by-name/recovery" > recovery_before.sha1`, then reboot to normal system and back into recovery, then `adb shell "sha1sum /dev/block/by-name/recovery" > recovery_after.sha1` and diff the two -- a change here only shows the mechanism ran, it still does not implicate /system/init.rc. 4) Check for run evidence from prior boots: `adb shell "cat /cache/recovery/last_install 2>/dev/null; ls -la /cache/recovery/ 2>/dev/null"` and, if pstore is present, `adb shell "cat /sys/fs/pstore/console-ramoops* 2>/dev/null | grep -i recovery"`. 5) Decisive check: if step 1 shows install-recovery.sh and/or recovery-from-boot.p are absent from this build (common on cheap Rockchip Go builds that skip the legacy recovery-update path entirely), the mechanism cannot run at all and this item is fully ruled out.
bypass_or_fix: Not applicable as a fix for the init.rc revert bug, because this mechanism does not write to /system/etc/init/hw/init.rc under any circumstance -- disabling it will not stop the observed revert. If it is nonetheless found present and you want to neutralize it for unrelated reasons (e.g. to stop it clobbering a custom recovery.img you flash later): `adb shell "chmod 000 $SYS/etc/install-recovery.sh"` (or delete it) so the oneshot service exec fails harmlessly instead of running applypatch, and/or remove the `service flash_recovery ...` block from init.rc, and/or delete `$SYS/recovery-from-boot.p` so applypatch has no patch data to work from (the script is designed to fail safe and only logs an error).
risk_level: Diagnostic test_procedure steps (ls/grep/sha1sum/cat) are read-only and zero-risk. The optional bypass steps (chmod/rm on install-recovery.sh, editing an init.rc service block, deleting recovery-from-boot.p) are low-risk and fully reversible; worst case is /recovery falling out of sync with /boot, a soft OTA-hygiene issue by design, not a bootability risk.
